known_facts_book1: A man of straw in Munchkin blue, with a painted cloth-bag face, one eye larger than the other and ears that are not mates.
Is met on the road of yellow bricks riding the Sawhorse, on his way to have Jinjur repaint his faded left ear, which had affected his hearing.
Falls into extravagant admiration of the Patchwork Girl at first sight and hurries back to the Emerald City to see more of her.
Has no heart and gets along perfectly well without one, unlike his friend the Tin Woodman.
Volunteers to be grabbed first when the party dashes past Mister Yoop's cave, knowing he is not fit to eat.
Is thrown at the marble picket fence by Hip Hopper, lands on top of a picket which catches him in the middle of the back, and hangs there kicking until a ladder is fetched.
Has the hole in his back and a ripped leg sewn up by Dorothy with the needle and thread from her knapsack.
Steers the raft on the Trick River with a broken branch and anchors it against a rock when the current reverses.
Lives in a castle in the Winkie Country near the Tin Woodman's palace, and often visits Dorothy at the royal palace.

known_facts_book1: Emperor of the Winkies, ruling the yellow country of Oz from a castle built entirely of tin by the Winkie tinsmiths.
Was once a flesh woodchopper who kept chopping himself with his axe and had each lost limb replaced with tin until he was all tin.
Keeps his tin body brilliantly polished and his joints well oiled, and has a valet who oils him.
His castle grounds hold tin fountains, tin flowers, tin trees and tin statues of Dorothy, Toto, the Scarecrow, the Wizard, the Shaggy Man, Jack Pumpkinhead and Ozma.
Owns a field of yellow lilies which the party must cross without treading on a single blossom.
Absolutely refuses to let anyone take the left wing of a yellow butterfly, calling it one of the most cruel and heartless deeds he ever heard of, and refuses even to lend a live butterfly.
Says he will protect his butterflies because he rules the Winkie Country, the only place in Oz where yellow butterflies are found.
Unknowingly supplies the drop of oil from a live man's body, which falls from his left knee-joint and is caught by Ojo in a crystal vial.
Argues Ojo out of his bad luck, declaring Friday is just one of seven days and thirteen is a lucky number, and renames him Ojo the Lucky.
Proposes that the whole party return to the Emerald City and ask Ozma's advice.

known_facts_book1: A big man shaggy in whiskers, eyebrows, hair, hat, laces, coat and breeches, with kindly blue eyes and a medallion of Princess Dorothy on his breast.
Came to Oz from the outside world with Dorothy and was allowed by Ozma to stay; he has a suite of rooms in the royal palace.
Rescues Ojo, Scraps, the Glass Cat and the Woozy from the great clutching leaves by whistling, which charms the plants, and by cutting the leaves with a dagger-shaped knife.
Carries condensed 'square meals' in tablet form, the invention of Professor Wogglebug of the Royal College of Athletics.
Knows the trick of the sliding road — walk backward — and the trick of the illusory wall between the Munchkin and green countries, which is passed with eyes shut.
Pins Chiss the giant porcupine under his foot after being struck by a quill, and has the quills gathered up and sunk in a pond.

Sings a song of his own composition naming Ozma, Dorothy, the Scarecrow, Nick Chopper, Professor Wogglebug, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Sawhorse, the Cowardly Lion, Tik-tok, the Hungry Tiger, Billina and the Nine Tiny Piglets.
Drives the live phonograph away by threatening to take it apart and scatter its pieces.

known_facts_book1: A man whose body is a framework of hickory branches dressed in a red spotted shirt, blue trousers, yellow vest and green-and-gold jacket, with a carved pumpkin set on a sharpened stick for a head.
Lives a day's journey from the Emerald City in a house made from the shell of an immense pumpkin, standing in the center of a vast pumpkin-field.
Was made by Tip and brought to life by Mombi with Dr. Pipt's Powder of Life, and is Ozma's earliest companion.
Uses pumpkin-seeds for brains and says he is intellectual only while they are fresh; he grows a whole field so he can select a new head when the old one spoils.
Carves the faces on his new heads himself, using the old face as a pattern.
Advises the party that a dark well must lie in the mountains of the Quadling Country, and tells the Scarecrow and Scraps about the Hoppers and the Horners.
Feeds the travellers vegetable soup, pumpkin pie and green cheese, and beds them on dried grasses.

known_facts_book1: A wooden horse whose body is a short length of log, its legs stout branches, its tail a small branch and its head a gnarled bump, with knots of wood for eyes.
Was brought to life by Tip with the Powder of Life and has been Ozma's favorite steed ever since.
Had no ears until the boy who owned him whittled two out of bark and stuck them in his head.
Has the bottoms of its legs shod with plates of gold by Ozma so the wood will not wear away, and a saddle of cloth-of-gold set with gems.
Has never worn a bridle, lives in a stable decorated with pearls and emeralds behind the royal palace, and is swift as the wind and untiring.
Kicks the Woozy squarely on the head with a gold-shod foot for sniffing at him.

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's little black shaggy dog with very bright eyes, her constant companion at the royal palace.
Cannot talk, being a common United States dog and not a fairy dog, but is understood by Dorothy.
Sniffs the Patchwork Girl once and lies down again, showing no interest in such an irregular creation.
Captures Hip Hopper the Champion by snapping at his single ankle until the wrestler loses his balance and falls.
Helps Dorothy rout the Tottenhots by barking and snapping at their bare legs.
Is held in Dorothy's arms during Ojo's trial in the Throne Room, where he is friends with the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger.
Spots the Quadling's house on the river bank that the others had missed.
